summary: Kyrgyzstan's Regulation on the stay of foreign citizens lets citizens of the countries in its Annex 1 — among them Australia, the UK, Germany, Canada, the US and Japan — stay visa-free for a total of 30 days in every 60-day period. It allows longer visa-free stays to some: up to 90 days in every 180 for citizens of Eurasian Economic Union states and of Serbia, Turkey, Ukraine, Mongolia and Moldova, up to 60 days in every 120 for Uzbekistan, and up to 180 days in every 360 for Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' e-Visa portal says citizens of certain countries are eligible for the e-Visa if they meet the required criteria.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says US dollars are the most easily exchanged foreign currency, that notes from before 2007 usually are not accepted or are subject to an additional charge when changing to Kyrgyz som, and that ATMs sometimes have a maximum som withdrawal limit.

The UK Foreign Office says that if you're visiting Kyrgyzstan for more than 30 calendar days, you must either leave before the 30 calendar day period ends or register online with the State Registration Service within 5 days of entry.

The UK Foreign Office says there is a basic mountain rescue service staffed by volunteers with limited rescue equipment, and that difficult terrain can in some circumstances make it impossible for emergency services to reach you. It advises getting adequate insurance, including for any activity at high altitude, using a reputable trekking agency, letting someone know when you plan to return and not trekking alone.

The Government of Canada says that, while limited cross-border travel between Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan is now possible, some checkpoints remain closed or restricted, and travellers may be subject to specific entry procedures and permit requirements.

The UK Foreign Office says to avoid flagging down taxis and to use licensed pre-ordered taxi services whenever possible, and to avoid local buses and minibuses if possible, as they are not always maintained properly and pickpockets operate on them.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Kyrgyzstan?
faq.answer: Kyrgyzstan's Regulation on the stay of foreign citizens lets citizens of the countries in its Annex 1 — among them Australia, the UK, Germany, Canada, the US and Japan — stay visa-free for a total of 30 days in every 60-day period; citizens of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain up to 180 days in every 360; citizens of Eurasian Economic Union states and of Serbia, Turkey, Ukraine, Mongolia and Moldova up to 90 days in every 180; and Uzbek citizens up to 60 days in every 120. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' e-Visa portal says you complete the online application and pay by card instead of applying through a Kyrgyz mission, and that citizens of certain countries are eligible if they meet the required criteria.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Kyrgyzstan visa-free?
faq.answer: Kyrgyzstan's Regulation on the stay of foreign citizens gives citizens of the countries in its Annex 1 a total of 30 days in every 60-day period, and the UK Foreign Office puts it, for British visitors, as stays of up to 30 calendar days without a visa for each 60-day period, after which UK nationals must either leave or obtain the appropriate documents.

faq.question: How does the Kyrgyzstan eVisa work?
faq.answer: The e-Visa portal says you complete the online application form and pay with a credit or debit card instead of applying through a Kyrgyz mission. It says the Tourist Visa (type "TS") is issued for short-term stays for tourism with a validity of up to 30 calendar days, and gives an application review period of 5 working days. It says the visa fee depends on visa category, type and period; no official source we could read states the amount.

faq.question: Do I need to register with the police in Kyrgyzstan?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says that if you're visiting Kyrgyzstan for more than 30 calendar days, you must either leave before the 30 calendar day period ends or register online with the State Registration Service within 5 days of entry, and that if you stay with someone who owns a property in Kyrgyzstan for longer than 30 calendar days, you and the property owner must register at the State Registration Service.

faq.question: Is Kyrgyzstan safe for trekking?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says trekking in Kyrgyzstan often involves travelling to very remote areas with a high risk of avalanches, landslides and rockfalls, that weather can change very quickly and there is a possibility of snow at higher altitudes even in summer, and that there is a basic mountain rescue service staffed by volunteers. It advises getting adequate insurance, including for any activity at high altitude, using a reputable trekking agency and not trekking alone.

countryFacts.payments.text: ATMs are widely available in main cities and usually distribute Kyrgyz som and US dollars. You should pay with KGS
ATMs sometimes have a maximum som withdrawal limit. This varies from bank to bank, but is often around 10,000 KGS.
Credit and debit cards are widely used around the country; VISA is accepted in most places, but MasterCard is sometimes not accepted. Payment by QR code is also common.
Bring cash if you plan to travel to rural areas where ATMs may not be available.

countryFacts.safety.text: Street crime is a risk, including bag-snatching and mugging. Take care if you go out alone or use public transport and consider using private cars or pre-arranged taxis at night.
There is a high risk of avalanches, landslides and rockfalls.
There is a high risk of earthquakes and tremors are frequent.

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: heavy snowfall can block roads and trekking routes, particularly in the autumn and winter
In the mountains, avalanches and landslides often block roads, particularly in the spring.
At higher altitudes there is a possibility of snow even in the summer months

entryRequirements.overstay.text: 1. Нарушение порядка пребывания, проживания или осуществления трудовой деятельности в Кыргызской Республике иностранными гражданами, выразившееся в отсутствии документов, подтверждающих право на пребывание в Кыргызской Республике (виза, регистрация, вид на жительство, свидетельство о регистрации ходатайства о признании беженцем, удостоверение беженца, разрешение на осуществление трудовой деятельности в случаях, предусмотренных законодательством в сфере внешней миграции), либо в использовании таких документов с истекшим сроком действия, либо в уклонении от выезда из Кыргызской Республики по истечении срока законного пребывания, в течение срока до одного месяца, - влечет наложение штрафа на физических лиц в размере 55 расчетных показателей. То же деяние, предусмотренное абзацем первым части 1 настоящей статьи, совершенное в течение срока: от одного до трех месяцев, - влечет наложение штрафа на физических лиц в размере 100 расчетных показателей; от трех до шести месяцев, - влечет наложение штрафа на физических лиц в размере 150 расчетных показателей; от шести месяцев до одного года, - влечет наложение штрафа на физических лиц в размере 175 расчетных показателей; более одного года, - влечет наложение штрафа на физических лиц в размере 200 расчетных показателей.

2. Иностранные граждане подлежат выдворению за пределы Кыргызской Республики за совершение правонарушений, связанных с нарушением порядка их пребывания в Кыргызской Республике, а также предусмотренных статьями 126-1 и 126-2 настоящего Кодекса, за исключением случаев, предусмотренных законодательством.
3. Выдворение иностранных граждан за пределы Кыргызской Республики как мера взыскания назначается судом.

entryRequirements.postArrivalRegistratio.text: If you’re visiting Kyrgyzstan for more than 30 calendar days, you must either leave the territory of Kyrgyzstan before the 30 calendar day period ends, or register online with the State Registration Service (SRS) (in Kyrgyz and Russian). You must register within 5 days of your entry into Kyrgyzstan for the period of your visa’s validity.

If you intend to stay in Kyrgyzstan for longer than 30 days, you must obtain an E-Visa before your arrival in the country. Once in the country, you must also register with the State Registration Service Passport Desk within 60 days following your arrival. You will need to show this proof of registration to leave the country. If you fail to do so, local authorities will prevent you from leaving until you pay the associated fine.
